---
title: "A logistic-regression analysis"
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

We now carry the SuperTelicity one-predictor analysis from raw counts to fitted probabilities. The scientific question is descriptive: how does *in* completion use differ between manner and result verbs in this sample?

```{r}
#| label: logistic-application-data
#| echo: true
st <- read.csv("data/supertelicity/supertelicity-cloze.csv")
st$verb_type <- factor(st$verb_type, levels = c("manner", "result"))
raw_counts <- as.data.frame(table(st$verb_type, st$preposition))
names(raw_counts) <- c("verb_type", "preposition", "observations")
raw_counts
```

```{r}
#| label: logistic-application-fit
#| echo: true
fit <- glm(prep_in ~ verb_type, family = binomial(), data = st)
groups <- aggregate(prep_in ~ verb_type, st, mean)
groups$n <- as.integer(table(st$verb_type))
link_prediction <- predict(fit, newdata = groups, se.fit = TRUE)
groups$fitted <- plogis(link_prediction$fit)
groups$lower <- plogis(link_prediction$fit - qnorm(.975) * link_prediction$se.fit)
groups$upper <- plogis(link_prediction$fit + qnorm(.975) * link_prediction$se.fit)
groups
```

The fit reproduces the higher sample probability for result verbs, and the plot places that raw contrast beside the row-independent GLM intervals. On the link scale, the likelihood is

$$
\ell(\boldsymbol\beta)=\sum_i\left[y_i\eta_i-
\log(1+e^{\eta_i})\right],
\qquad \eta_i=\beta_0+\beta_1\operatorname{result}_i.
$$

```{r}
#| label: logistic-application-plot
#| echo: true
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(groups, aes(verb_type, prep_in)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), color = "#1F5A85") +
  geom_point(size = 2.3) +
  labs(x = "Verb type", y = "Probability of an in-completion") +
  theme_classic()
```

Maximizing it yields the coefficient estimates printed below.

```{r}
#| label: logistic-application-coefficients
#| echo: true
summary(fit)$coefficients
```

The intervals shown are the row-independent GLM intervals and are included to expose the mechanics. They are not the inferential result of the source paper. The rows reuse participants and sentence materials, and the original analysis models that dependence. Nor does the observed contrast show that verb type causes a completion choice.
